category_title: Probationary high school students with severe behavioral challenges and academic resistance
minimal_context: The student is asked to complete an end-of-period world history test to recall what they learned during the class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is the end of the period. Please take this world history test and write down what you remember from today's lesson.

STUDENT: (Talks with another student and throws a pen cap across the room) I'm not doing that.

TUTOR: Please look at the test and try your best.

STUDENT: (Tears a page out of the history book and tags it) Whatever.

TUTOR: We need to see what you learned today. Just write down something.

STUDENT: I remember nothing you taught and I refuse to take any tests.

options.A: Concentrate on the long-term teaching of a small repertoire of reading strategies, such as predicting, questioning, imagining, clarifying, and summarizing.
options.B: Grade the student's recreated historical artifacts over time using a rubric based on state art curriculum standards.
options.C: Guide the student to progressively tune their awareness to each body part, intentionally relaxing each part from their toes to their head.
options.D: Require the student to use a digital note-taking application to take notes, organize their history work, and archive past projects.
